name: Saccular Spinal Dysraphism with a Stalk to the Dome

criteria.description: Presence of a visible saccular mass on the dorsal midline of the spine
Identification of a fibrous stalk connecting the spinal cord to the dome of the sac
MRI evidence showing the stalk and associated spinal cord abnormalities
Presence of neurological deficits consistent with spinal cord tethering

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a visible saccular mass with MRI confirmation of a stalk connecting the spinal cord to the dome
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; histopathology may assist post-surgically.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visible dorsal midline saccular mass with stalk connection
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic external sac with stalk connecting to spinal cord
searchTerms: visible sac-like mass on back with stalk
dorsal midline skin cyst with connection
skin mass on spine with stalk

pathognomonic.notes: Neurological symptoms due to abnormal cord fixation

common.notes: Variable degrees of paresis or paralysis

searchTerms: cutaneous signs on top of lesion
sensory loss in feet and legs

occasional.notes: Fluid-filled cavities within the spinal cord

rare.notes: Increased intracranial pressure due to CSF flow obstruction
Ulceration due to sac rupture or infection
searchTerms: skin sores or ulcers over sacral area
open skin wounds on lower back

rare.notes: Occasional seizures secondary to associated CNS anomalies

imaging: MRI demonstrating a saccular dorsal spinal mass with stalk connecting to spinal cord
Ultrasound in neonates showing cystic spinal lesion
CT scan may show bony defects in posterior vertebral elements
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathology of excised sac shows fibrous stalk and neural elements

distinguishingFeatures: Open neural tube defect with exposed neural tissue
Absence of stalk connecting spinal cord to dome
More severe neurological deficits at birth
Presence of lipomatous tissue within the spinal canal
Fatty mass rather than clear stalk

redFlags: Signs of sac rupture or infection
references: Kothbauer KF. Spinal dysraphism with a stalk to the dome: clinical and surgical considerations. Neurosurg Focus. 2010;29(1):E6.
Talamonti G, et al. Saccular spinal dysraphism: diagnosis and management. Childs Nerv Syst. 2015;31(5):765-774.
